2rude.bio:
Toronto producer, songwriter and label founder Richard Coombs, better known as 2Rude, occupies an important place in the infrastructure of late-1990s and early-2000s Canadian hip-hop and R&B. Working through Rudimental Records, he built records around Canadian voices at a moment when domestic rap and R&B still had limited major-label support. His production on Maestro's 1998 single "Stick to Your Vision" helped return one of Canadian hip-hop's foundational artists to the charts, while collaborations with singers and rappers across Toronto's scene made 2Rude a connective figure between hip-hop, soul and reggae-influenced urban music.

His 1999 compilation album Rudimental 2K made that network the point. The project paired Canadian performers with established U.S. guests and included "Thinkin' About You," featuring Snow, Smoothe da Hustler, Miranda and Latoya Walsh. The song won the 2000 Juno Award for Best R&B/Soul Recording, while "Dissin' Us," featuring Grimmi Grimmi and Jully Black, earned a MuchMusic Video Award. Rather than functioning only as a behind-the-scenes beatmaker, 2Rude used the album and his label to create a platform where Canadian rap and R&B artists could appear together at scale.

That role is central to his significance. 2Rude's catalogue intersects with Maestro, Saukrates, Jully Black, Glenn Lewis, Eternia and other artists who helped turn Toronto's urban-music community into a sustainable national scene. His work illustrates how Canadian hip-hop grew not only through breakthrough MCs but through producers, independent labels and collaborative records that gave emerging artists room to develop and cross genre lines.
2rude.directory_summary: Toronto producer and Rudimental Records founder 2Rude helped build the connective tissue of Canadian hip-hop and R&B in the late 1990s and early 2000s. His Rudimental 2K project brought Canadian and U.S. artists together, while "Thinkin' About You" won the 2000 Juno for Best R&B/Soul Recording. His work with Maestro, Jully Black, Saukrates and others made him an important behind-the-scenes architect of Toronto's urban-music ecosystem.

4korners.bio:
Toronto DJ, producer and recording artist Kirk St. Cyr, known professionally as 4KORNERS, built his reputation by treating the DJ booth as both a performance role and a platform for Canadian music. He became the Toronto Raptors' official DJ in the mid-2000s and grew with the franchise from arena resident to a recognizable part of its game-night identity, later handling the 2016 NBA All-Star Game in Toronto. At the same time, an international club and event schedule took him well beyond Canada, giving him a global frame of reference while keeping Toronto at the centre of his work.

His recorded output gradually moved that curatorial identity into original production. Singles and the Changes EP marked the transition, but the 2022 debut album 4KORNERS of the World made the concept explicit: hip-hop, electronic music, Afrobeats, dancehall, soca and other club forms presented as a reflection of Toronto's multicultural character and of what he had absorbed while touring. The project also foregrounded emerging Canadian artists including EverythingOShauN, Odreii, Ashton Adams and Temia, extending his long-standing interest in using high-visibility DJ spaces to introduce audiences to new domestic music.

4KORNERS matters in Canadian music because his career sits at the intersection of nightlife, professional sports, diaspora culture and artist development. For years, Raptors games gave him one of the country's largest recurring stages for music curation, while his production work turned that experience into a catalogue shaped by Toronto's unusually broad mix of sounds. His trajectory shows how a DJ can function not only as an entertainer but as a cultural connector between scenes, audiences and generations of Canadian artists.
4korners.directory_summary: Toronto DJ and producer 4KORNERS has spent years connecting Canadian music, nightlife and basketball culture as the Toronto Raptors' official DJ. His 2022 debut album 4KORNERS of the World translated that global club experience into a genre-spanning portrait of multicultural Toronto, with emerging Canadian artists placed at the centre. His significance lies as much in curation and platform-building as in production: he has used major stages to introduce audiences to new domestic music.

88glam.bio:
Toronto rappers Derek Wise and 88Camino formed 88GLAM in 2017 after both had developed solo identities around the city's Get Home Safe circle. Their self-titled debut mixtape arrived that year with the NAV collaboration "Bali" and the single "12," establishing a nocturnal sound built from melodic trap, R&B phrasing and icy production. The project entered the Canadian albums chart and helped place the duo within the broader wave of Toronto rap that was reaching international audiences through streaming and the city's increasingly influential label ecosystem.

The pair signed with XO and Republic and followed with 88GLAM2 in 2018, featuring NAV and Gunna. The period brought four Juno nominations across 2019 and 2020, including Breakthrough Group of the Year, Group of the Year and Rap Recording of the Year recognition. Their music refined a specific late-2010s Toronto aesthetic: woozy synths, luxury imagery, melodic flows and trap production that sounded connected to the city without simply reproducing the work of its biggest stars.

After separating from XO and Republic, 88GLAM continued independently and eventually released Close to Heaven Far from God in 2022, their final album as a duo. Their run was relatively short, but it captured an important transition in Canadian rap, when Toronto artists could move quickly from local online momentum to global streaming audiences. 88GLAM's catalogue remains a useful snapshot of that era and of the network linking Get Home Safe, XO, NAV and the city's melodic-trap scene.
88glam.directory_summary: Toronto duo 88GLAM, formed by Derek Wise and 88Camino, helped define the city's late-2010s melodic-trap sound. Their self-titled debut and 88GLAM2 turned the NAV-assisted "Bali" and other atmospheric records into national momentum, leading to four Juno nominations across 2019 and 2020. Though the duo's run ended after 2022's Close to Heaven Far from God, their catalogue captures a key moment when Toronto rap was becoming a global streaming force.
